text:
Dubai registered 11,316 residential sales worth AED 33,892,693,593 in the last four weeks, a 7.0 percent increase in volume and 23.3 percent rise in value compared to the prior period. Mortgage registrations totaled 4,572, recorded separately from sales. The median residential price per square foot reached AED 1,693, up 1.1 percent from the previous four weeks. Off-plan transactions accounted for 58.0 percent of sales, down from 61.5 percent in the preceding period.

Rental activity showed 89,438 Ejari contracts with a renewal share of 51.8 percent. The median residential rent stood at AED 69,498 per year. Top performing areas by sales volume over twelve weeks include Dubai South with 3,433 transactions and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,299. Dubai South recorded a median price of AED 1,690 per square foot, while Jumeirah Village Circle averaged AED 1,435 per square foot.

Pricing momentum varied significantly across communities. Al Yufrah 1 saw a 43.3 percent increase in median price per square foot over twelve weeks, followed by Dubai Industrial City at 12.5 percent. Conversely, Palm Jumeirah cooled with a 14.0 percent decline, and Liwan dropped 13.4 percent. Highest estimated gross yields were found in Zaabeel First at 9.0 percent and International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent.

Investors should monitor the 1,048 anomalous sales flagged in the last 60 days, which deviated more than 35 percent from comparable medians. These figures derive from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, mortgages, gifts, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
